segments.t: Rebuffed at the supply desk, rookie Baek Seung-chan returns to the 2 Days & 1 Night office. He finds Ra Joon-mo and writer Ji-yeon debating wrap-party seating, and ends up taking a strange command literally. Listen for "isyu", the English word 'issue', and "heundeulda", 'to shake'.
지난번 회식 때 텐션 장난 아니었거든요.
지금 출력을 못 하는데 빨리 가서 받아와.
Let's unpack those fourteen lines of office miscommunication.
'What risk?' Joon-mo asks about the problem using "museun", 'what kind of', before "riseukeu", the English word 'risk'.
'The seating arrangement issue.' Ji-yeon points out the "jari baechi", 'seating arrangement'. She ends with "isyujyo", blending the English word 'issue' with a polite ending.
지난번 회식 때 텐션 장난 아니었거든요.

'The tension was no joke at the last team dinner.' "Jinanbeon" means 'last time', and "hoesik" is a company dinner. Saying "jangnan anieotgeodeunyo" literally means it was 'no joke', explaining how bad the tension was.

'They said no because we took one last month.' Returning empty-handed, Seung-chan reports "an doendaeyo", 'they say it is not allowed'. The supply room claimed they "badagatdago", 'took and went', one "jeobeon dal", 'last month'.
'What are you talking about?' Joon-mo snaps back with "mwon soriya?", a casual 'what sound is that?' used when someone says nonsense.
지금 출력을 못 하는데 빨리 가서 받아와.

'We can't print right now, so go quickly and get it.' "Jigeum" means 'right now', and "chullyeogeul mot haneunde" explains they are unable to print. He orders the rookie to "bada wa", 'receive and come back'.
'Did you shake the toner?' He asks "heundeureosseoyo?", the polite past form of 'to shake', wondering if Seung-chan tried the classic office trick.
'Pardon?' Startled, Seung-chan replies with "ne?", which means 'yes' but acts as 'pardon?' when asked as a question.
'I asked if you shook the toner.' Joon-mo repeats himself using "-nyago", an ending that quotes a question: 'I am asking if...'.
'No, not me, no.' Seung-chan stammers "aniyo", polite 'no', and "jeoneun", 'as for me', thinking he is being accused of breaking something.
'Try shaking it.' Joon-mo tells him "heundeureobwayo", combining 'shake' and 'try', hoping to squeeze out a few more pages.
'What are you doing over there?' Catching him later, Joon-mo asks "mwohani?", a casual 'what are you doing?', pointing at "geogiseo", 'over there'.
'Because you told me to try shaking the toner...' Seung-chan trails off with "-haeseo", 'because you said', quoting the earlier command.

'We already shook that one as much as it could be shaken.' Joon-mo sighs that "geugeo", 'that thing', has already been shaken "mankeum", 'as much as', possible. Now let's listen to the whole toner incident again.
지난번 회식 때 텐션 장난 아니었거든요.
지금 출력을 못 하는데 빨리 가서 받아와.
You heard "hoesik" for a team dinner, "mwon soriya?" for 'what are you talking about?', and "heundeulda" for shaking something. Catch you next time!

lines.fragment: 지금 출력을 못하는데 빨리 가서 받아와
